statements.quote: We introduce Epitome (www.epitome-ai.com), an open experimental platform that operationalizes this paradigm through Matrix-like social worlds where researchers can study isolated human subjects and groups interacting with LLM agents.
statements.locator: p. 1, Abstract; platform link.

statements.quote: We introduce Epitome (www.epitome-ai.com), the first open experimental platform designed for this new social reality.
statements.locator: p. 2, Introduction; platform link.

statements.quote: The experiment management module enables users to reference and modify existing, open-source social experiments to create and iterate their own experiments. Meanwhile, the open feature promotes knowledge sharing and enhances research transparency and reproducibility.
statements.locator: p. 3, Results, Platform architecture enables flexible human-AI experimentation.

statements.quote: Module I: Epitome provides users with experiment management and an open-source experiment community.
statements.locator: p. 5, Fig. 1 caption, Module I.

statements.quote: Module III: In the experiment preparation phase, Epitome supports multiple types of experimental interventions including text, images, videos, and audio, as well as questionnaire design. The module provides multimodal large language models as well, enabling users to generate more targeted materials using text-to-image and image-to-video capabilities.
statements.locator: p. 5, Fig. 1 caption, Module III; experimental materials generation.

statements.quote: In the data collection and analysis phase, Epitome offers data download and visualization capabilities, presenting experimental results through diverse chart formats for comprehensive result display.
statements.locator: p. 5, Fig. 1 caption; data export capability.

statements.quote: The Data Download and Analysis phase supports users in batch downloading data packages and utilizing multiple data visualization methods, providing the integrated capacity of data processing and analyzing.
statements.locator: p. 6, Results, platform workflow.

statements.quote: Epitome establishes three types of experimental environment (see in Fig.1a Module VII and Supplementary Section G for details) to enable ethically sensitive or high-risk experiments within a controlled space isolated from actual society, thereby minimizing unintended consequences32.
statements.locator: p. 6, Reducing the Scope of Inaccessible Research by LLM-driven Simulation; Supplementary Section G.

statements.quote: Concurrent with this, Epitome’s integrated analytical pipeline, including multi-modal data integration, batch retrieval, and advanced visualization methods (see details of Supplementary Section G) generates actionable insights to guide on-the-fly cohort reconfiguration, while its web-based interface allows participants worldwide to access the experiment.
statements.locator: p. 7, Supporting a Paradigm Shift to Integrated Experiment Design; Supplementary Section G.

statements.quote: Furthermore, Epitome facilitates the conduct of long-term, granular multimodal data collection, encompassing comprehensive human-AI interaction records, real-time model parameter tracking, and audio-visual screen recordings.
statements.locator: p. 7, Supporting a Paradigm Shift to Integrated Experiment Design; data collection.

statements.quote: Finally, Epitome exposes multi-flow experimental structures and fine-grained conditional control over tasks, interface states and agent behavior, with all condition logic and event sequences logged.
statements.locator: p. 8, Ensuring Causal Validity through Rigorous Experimental Control; condition and event logging.

statements.quote: Epitome simplifies research workflows with its Canvas-Based Interactive Design, merging the traditional four-phase, twelve-task process into a unified pipeline (see Supplementary Section A).
statements.locator: p. 8, paragraph following Epitome supports four primary research modes.

statements.quote: To facilitate experimental replication in Case Study 1, Epitome embeds large language model dialogue capabilities within the survey, thereby enriching human–AI interaction and streamlining data collection.
statements.locator: p. 9, Fig. 2 caption, panel c.

statements.quote: In addition, Epitome captured granular interaction data that are typically difficult to obtain in online field experiments. Real-time data tracking is implemented within the Data Collection module, automatic logging of all interaction events reduces measurement error and supports fine-grained compliance checks63.
statements.locator: p. 10, Productivity effects of generative AI, first paragraph.

statements.quote: Leveraging Epitome’s built-in instrumentation, we find that AI assistance reduces completion time by 37% (t = −4.06, p < 0.01, df = 68; Supplementary Figure 9) and improves output quality by 18% (t = 3.18, p < 0.01, df = 68; Supplementary Figure 10).
statements.locator: p. 10, Productivity effects of generative AI, second paragraph; Supplementary Figures 9-10.

statements.quote: Participants report enhanced self-efficacy (t = 2.81, p < 0.01, df = 68; Supplementary Figure 11) and greater task enjoyment (t = 2.83, p < 0.01, df = 68; Supplementary Figure 12), while broader perceptions of AI remain statistically unchanged (t = 1.37, p = 0.181, df = 33; Supplementary Figure 13), suggesting that short-term use primarily shifts performance and local experience rather than deep-seated attitudes (Noy & Zhang, 2023).
statements.locator: p. 10, Productivity effects of generative AI, second paragraph; Supplementary Figures 11-13.

statements.quote: The Dify-based low-code workflow supports the experimental design in Case Study 2, particularly by limiting the number of AI-generated ideas and streamlining the distribution of experimental materials.
statements.locator: p. 11, Fig. 3 caption, panel c.

statements.quote: Our results confirm a significant boost in individual creativity—increasing by 42.1% with 1 AI idea (T-test result: t = 5.30, p < 0.01, df = 149) and 16.4% with 5 AI ideas (T-test result: t = 2.52, p < 0.05, df = 149), particularly for lower-baseline creators (see Supplementary Figure 21-22 for details).
statements.locator: p. 12, Human creativity and generative AI, first paragraph; Supplementary Figures 21-22.

statements.quote: Real-time tracking revealed how AI ideas influence creative processes, providing insights more difficult to obtain without integrated experimental tools.
statements.locator: p. 12, Human creativity and generative AI, second paragraph.

statements.quote: The automatic Data Collection module offers insights into the dynamics of moral reasoning and thus enables the identification of a consistent bias towards justice in the AI's decision-making. AI agents consistently favored justice-based reasoning across iterations (Supplementary Table 2-3).
statements.locator: p. 12, Moral reasoning in human-AI interactions; data collection and Supplementary Tables 2-3.

statements.quote: Sentiment remained stable (7/10) regardless of scenario complexity (Supplementary Figure 33a-33b).
statements.locator: p. 12, Moral reasoning in human-AI interactions; Supplementary Figures 33a-33b.

statements.quote: Female participants showed greater leniency (T-test result: t = 2.24, p < 0.05, df = 10), reflecting gendered moral priorities (Supplementary Figure 33c-33d).
statements.locator: p. 12, Moral reasoning in human-AI interactions; Supplementary Figures 33c-33d.

statements.quote: Epitome is the first Real-Time Human-AI Social Experiments platform (Supplementary Figure 34).
statements.locator: p. 14, Discussion, second paragraph; Supplementary Figure 34.

statements.quote: Further information on research design is available in the Nature Research Reporting Summary linked to this article.
statements.locator: p. 16, Reporting summary.

statements.quote: Third, a database and knowledge-base management system provides traceability of experimental data and knowledge artifacts, underpinning data analysis, reproducibility, and validation.
statements.locator: p. 16, Materials and Methods, Technical Implementations.

statements.quote: The detailed data of the case studies in the paper and related materials associated with the experiments are available in Supplementary Information.
statements.locator: p. 18, Data, Materials, Software Availability, sentence 1.

statements.quote: For more and latest information, refer to GitHub - epitome-AISS/epitome.
statements.locator: p. 18, Data, Materials, Software Availability, sentence 2; hyperlink https://github.com/epitome-AISS/epitome.

statements.quote: Moreover, a user manual for all experiment designers is provided, offering detailed guidance on the functions and operational procedures of the Epitome platform (see Supplementary Section G).
statements.locator: p. 18, Data, Materials, Software Availability, sentence 3.

statements.quote: Epitome platform now uses a managed access model, interested researchers who wish to use Epitome to support their experiments are encouraged to contact the authors for access.
statements.locator: p. 18, Data, Materials, Software Availability, sentence 4; managed access refers to platform use.

statements.quote: For application or accession, refer to www.epitome-ai.com.
statements.locator: p. 18, Data, Materials, Software Availability, sentence 5; hyperlink https://www.epitome-ai.com/.

statements.quote: The Epitome platform integrates its multiple tasks into a single platform based on the B/S architecture, providing a user-friendly web interface that allows researchers and participants to both log in and use the system.
statements.locator: p. 16, Materials and Methods, Technical Implementations; platform login.

statements.quote: The platform implements a four-tier framework: (1) informed consent mechanisms that clearly disclose when participants interact with AI agents; (2) data minimization protocols that collect only information essential to research questions; (3) transparency features that allow participants to review and understand AI-generated responses; and (4) oversight mechanisms that facilitate IRB review of experimental designs.
statements.locator: pp. 17-18, Four-Tier Framework for Epitome’s Ethical Safeguard Strategy; data minimization and transparency.

statements.quote: 56. Bisbee, J., Clinton, J., Dorff, C., Kenkel, B. & Larson, J. Synthetic replacements for human survey data? The perils of large language models. Preprint at https://doi.org/10.31235/osf.io/5ecfa (2023).
statements.locator: p. 22, References, reference 56; OSF-hosted cited preprint, unrelated to c885 study-data availability.

deposits.notes:
Named on PDF p. 18 and in form data_and_code.code_url. The repository web page and recursive-tree API both returned HTTP 200. Inspected HEAD commit 7a0ee3b675e12748bccc0943524a86a2b9d6f841; tree truncated=false. n_files=595 counts all repository blobs, including 63 Excel workbooks under data/experiment_data and platform source code. The files list is limited to 50 entries (46 data workbooks plus LICENSE, two READMEs and pom.xml); every one of the 63 data workbooks was read in memory, all with HTTP 200, totaling 646785 bytes.

The four data directories are Productivity effects of GenAI (Replication of the Experiment)-1_CA-Control-1, -1_CA-Treatment-1, -1_EA-Control-1 and -1_EA-Treatment-1. These identify the productivity replication (S1), with Control/Treatment and convex/exact-time subgroups. Arm labels are encoded in directory names, not in a separate spreadsheet column; their interpretation as Overleaf/ChatGPT follows the paper's S1 design and Treatment-only ChatGPT-use questionnaires. No independent randomization manifest is supplied.

rows_checked=50 is the number of data rows, excluding the header, in each Task A or Task B sheet (sheet '0'), not the number of analyzed people. Every questionnaire export and user.xlsx has 50 userName rows but only five rows with questionnaire answers/timing or user metadata. Each of the eight task sheets contains five nonempty Q1 writing outputs, for 40 outputs in total. The same five userName identifiers occur in Task A and Task B within each directory. Across the four directories there are 20 distinct identifiers with task responses (10 Control-labelled and 10 Treatment-labelled). These are observed exported identifiers, not verified randomized or analyzed sample counts. The paper reports 35 analyzed people for S1, so these files cannot establish the complete analysis sample or its arm sizes. Whether the released records are a subset or demonstration export is undocumented.

Q1 in the task sheets contains substantive English workplace emails about organizational restructuring at AccureCo or adoption of WorkCo's virtual office. userName links outputs across tasks and questionnaires. materialGroupUseRecord.xlsx contains HTML task instructions in data, with 10 nonempty records per directory; materialId and materialName are empty. Other exports contain generic Q1-Q11 response columns for screening, demographics, consent, time use, efficacy, completion and ChatGPT-use questions. No identifiable expert writing-quality, content-quality, originality or headline quality/creativity ratings, rater IDs, inclusion/exclusion flags, scoring codebook or analysis script was found. has_outcome_scores=false refers to the screened creativity/quality outcomes, not the presence of task timing or self-reported questionnaire responses.

No S2 adventure-story corpus, language assignments, AI-suggestion arms, creativity ratings or diversity-analysis files were present in the complete repository tree. No S3 data were identified. GitHub releases API returned HTTP 200 with zero releases; branches API returned HTTP 200 with only main. The README identifies the paper but does not document these data exports or supply the cited Supplementary Information.

The repository LICENSE is MIT for software and associated documentation; the README also states MIT. No separate license specific to participant data was identified.

notes:
Checked 2026-10-10. Read all 322 lines of the saved markdown, including all references; the saved PDF has 25 pages, ends with references and has zero embedded files. All statement quotations were copied from PyMuPDF text, with whitespace/line breaks normalized; punctuation and non-ASCII characters were preserved. The paper cites separate Supplementary Information and a Nature Research Reporting Summary, but neither is included in the supplied document. No preregistration statement or separate acknowledgment-based data offer was found.

The only dataset-bearing deposit identified is the named GitHub repository. Directly verified public S1 output/participant-linked exports justify public_partial. Their coverage is not sufficient for the missing full-study statistics in final.open_items, so what_we_could_compute is null. For the released S1 subset one could count nonempty records by exported group, link repeated task outputs, compute timing summaries, and construct new within-group text-diversity measures. These would describe the released records only. They do not establish published-study analyzed counts, reconstruct expert-score arm means/SDs/SEs, determine rating aggregation or exclusions, or recover S2's individual-creativity/diversity results, arm/language counts, language overlap, or 31-story coverage.

https://www.epitome-ai.com/ returned HTTP 200, but its unauthenticated response was a JavaScript application shell titled Epitome with no supplementary-file links. The p. 18 request-for-access language explicitly concerns running experiments on the platform; it is not a statement that the study data are available on request. No account was created, no login attempted and no access request sent.

The available publication landing page, https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.01061, returned HTTP 200. It lists v3, revised 24 December 2025, 25 pages and six figures, but no journal publication or separate supplementary data file. The v1 and v2 landing pages also returned HTTP 200 and did not supply separate supplements. The linked v2 source archive https://arxiv.org/src/2507.01061v2 returned HTTP 200 (3578737 bytes), was read only in memory, and contained 10 files: manuscript/style/bibliography/README components and five single-page figure/table PDFs. Inspection of those PDFs found platform illustrations/comparisons, not participant data or the missing supplement. The older manuscript source points to the same GitHub repository. These older materials were not used to replace the saved-paper results.

The OSF DOI in bibliography reference 56, https://doi.org/10.31235/osf.io/5ecfa, returned HTTP 200 and redirected to https://osf.io/5ecfa_v1. It identifies Bisbee and colleagues' unrelated preprint Synthetic replacements for human survey data? The perils of large language models, not a deposit of c885 participants; it is excluded from deposits. Other bibliography citations are not evidence of c885 data availability.

Search records distinguish API result totals from relevant c885 data deposits. Zenodo's initial size=100 requests failed with HTTP 400 because the unauthenticated limit is 25; successful size=25 repeats are recorded. No credentials or identifiers beyond the required atlas-screening/0.1 User-Agent were sent. Broad Epitome keyword searches were sampled and then narrowed; the full-title and first-author searches across all four prescribed APIs found no additional study-data deposit. Confidence is high in the partial-data classification based on direct inspection of all 63 public workbooks; completeness of the published analysis sample remains unverified.
